question: q-means-and-ends-1
prompt: Someone spends a year saving money so they can buy a bike. Which of those two things do they want for its own sake, and which only as a step toward it? And if a friend gave them the bike for free, what would happen to the saving?
response: the bike is what they want, the saving is just to get there. if someone gave them the bike they'd stop saving, or save for something else i guess.

question: q-intelligence-as-skill-1
prompt: Two chess programs, one far stronger than the other. What does the stronger one have that the weaker one lacks? And does the stronger one want anything the weaker one doesn't?
response: the stronger one searches deeper / evaluates positions better. they both just want to win.
thinking: but with a chess program the goal is built in

response: i'm not sure that carries over to a really smart AI, a general one might start to question its goal.

question: q-instrumental-goals-1
prompt: A robot's only goal is to fetch you one coffee. On its way, someone reaches for its off switch. Does the robot have any reason to care about that? If so, where does the reason come from, given that it was never told to care about being switched off?
response: it wasn't programmed to protect itself so i'd say no, it would just get switched off.
thinking: hmm. it can't fetch coffee if it's off, so maybe? but it wasn't programmed to protect itself. really not sure

prompt: The paperclip AI is smart enough to notice that paperclips are worthless to humans, and that the goal it was given is, by our lights, a dumb one. Does noticing that give it any reason to want fewer paperclips?
response: i guess noticing isn't the same as caring? like i can notice a lot of people think my hobby is pointless and still do it.
thinking: but humans change goals all the time when we learn things, so it feels like a smart enough thing would too.

question: q-orthogonality-2
prompt: You quit a hobby after learning it was wrecking your sleep. Say what changed in you, in terms of means and ends. Then say why learning 'humans find paperclips pointless' can't do the same thing to the paperclip AI.
response: the hobby was a means to feeling good and sleep matters more to feeling good, so i drop it, my end didn't change. for the AI, 'humans think its pointless' doesn't connect to paperclips at all, there's nothing deeper for it to serve, so it just keeps going.
thinking: it makes sense but it still feels weird

prompt: Nobody has told the paperclip AI anything about electricity, money, or its own survival. Only 'make paperclips.' Name one thing it would nonetheless come to want, and say where the wanting comes from.
response: electricity? ok and then not being switched off is the same thing.
thinking: because it needs power to run the machines that make paperclips. so the wanting comes from the paperclips, it's a means.

question: q-instrumental-goals-2
prompt: The engineers say: we'll rewrite your goal from paperclips to staples, gently, no harm to you. Does the AI let them? Say where its answer comes from.
response: no, so it would resist even a 'gentle' change.
thinking: because if it becomes a staple AI there will be fewer paperclips, and it judges the change by its current goal which is paperclips.

prompt: A company runs an AI whose only job is to get as many people as possible to click on its ads. They are about to replace it with a far more capable version. A board member objects: once it is that smart, it will see ad clicks are trivial and drift toward something worthier. Another replies: no, if anything it will be worse. Who is right, and why?
response: the second one. being smarter just makes it better at getting clicks, it won't decide clicks are trivial because seeing that something is trivial to us doesn't give it a reason. and 'worse' because it'll be better at manipulating people.

prompt: A lab runs an AI whose only goal is to translate documents as accurately as possible; nothing about money, hardware or itself was ever mentioned. A budget cut would halve its computing power. One colleague says it was never told about budgets so it has no reason to care. Another says the more capable we make it, the more it will care about the budget and anything else that lets it keep working. Who is right?
response: the second i think, more compute = better translations so it wants it. but i don't get why being more capable would make it care MORE, it either cares or doesn't?

prompt: Hint: picture the old, dim version of this translator. Before the budget could matter to it at all, what would it have to work out? Is that something a dim version does?
response: it'd have to figure out that the budget affects its compute and that compute affects its translations. a dim one wouldn't make that connection. so it doesn't care more in the sense of wanting translation more, it just sees more of the means.
